title: run.skill.md: no guidance that run_command uses cmd.exe on Windows; agents incorrectly use PowerShell syntax
description: run_command on Windows executes commands through cmd.exe, not PowerShell. run.skill.md contains no explicit guidance on which shell is used, so agents default to PowerShell cmdlets (e.g. Get-ChildItem, Sort-Object, Select-Object) in run_command calls. These fail with 'not recognized as an internal or external command' because cmd.exe cannot execute PowerShell cmdlets. The correct approach is to use cmd.exe-compatible syntax (e.g. dir, type, findstr) on Windows and sh-compatible syntax on Unix. Observed in the moeb.run-skill-tool-improvement-signal run where Get-ChildItem and Sort-Object calls failed and had to be retried with dir /O-D /B.
proposed_resolution: Add explicit guidance in run.skill.md (e.g. in Phase 3 tool-use notes or the Tool Origin Policy section) stating: run_command uses cmd.exe on Windows and sh on Unix. Agents must use shell-appropriate syntax — cmd commands on Windows (dir, type, findstr, etc.), sh-compatible commands on Unix — and must not use PowerShell cmdlets in run_command calls regardless of the host environment.
